unit.title: AST Traversal as an Engineering Component
unit.scope: A self-contained Rust exercise in designing, testing, and documenting a deterministic AST traversal and outline renderer.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building practical software-engineering habits.
prerequisites: Data structures, including trees and recursive traversal
Working knowledge of Rust ownership, enums, pattern matching, and Cargo
learning_objectives: Turn a traversal requirement into explicit, testable invariants
Separate tree walking from output policy so each can evolve independently
Produce deterministic behavior and tests for nested and empty structures
Use Rust error handling, documentation, and reproducible command evidence
State integration assumptions without pretending compatibility with unavailable KECC APIs
deliverables: A buildable Rust crate implementing the assigned miniature AST traversal
Automated tests, including exact-output and structural coverage cases
DESIGN.md documenting invariants, ownership choices, and integration assumptions
EVIDENCE.md recording commands actually run and their results
Written responses to the comprehension prompts
out_of_scope: Claiming to implement or match the KECC repository API
SSA construction, IR optimization, or RISC-V code generation

requires: A validator controlled by the worker harness independently builds and tests the submission
The independent examiner rubric is applied to the submitted evidence
No unavailable external material is represented as reviewed or completed
completion_policy.prohibited_inference: Acceptance of this unit is evidence only for this bounded kickoff; it is never evidence that CS420, its official homework, recordings, textbooks, or later compiler stages were completed.
